rationale:
OWNER RULING 2026-08-17, on RFC_033: build the source-scan lockstep, NOT a single mandatory entrypoint. RFC_033 was opened at this council's own architecture seat's direction on the bugs_closed/285 fix (corr 79f70435, APPROVED with ARCHITECTURE_SIGNAL: needs_rfc): the two new datahelpers symbols are a cross-package contract with no enforced call path, so 'a future section-list consumer can still be written lock-blind exactly as the original bug arose'. The seat recommended proceeding and opening the RFC in parallel, which is what happened; this is the ruled half.

WHAT IT DOES. One test file. It scans actions/, actions/*/ and datahelpers/ for files that read site_plan_sections (FROM or JOIN), and requires each either to call the merge (LoadLockedPageSlots/MergeLockedPageSlots) or to be declared in lockBlindPlanReaders WITH A REASON. Population measured 2026-08-17 by running the detector: 6 readers, 2 merge, 4 declared. It failed on first run and found a fifth reader (discovery_checks/check_sectionless_pages.go) that my own hand census had missed because I had only grepped FROM, not JOIN — i.e. the mechanism justified itself before it was committed.

WHY site_plan_sections AND NOT pages.sections. The plan is the store that structurally cannot know about a lock; the cache now carries the merged list (live v1.0.1305, proven on natural rebuilds of loancalculator.co.uk/index 08-16 and webdesign.uk/contact 08-17), so a cache reader gets locked rows for free and needs no declaration. Scoping to the cache too would fire on ~18 files and teach authors to add a line to a list rather than think, which is the failure mode of a census that cries wolf.

WHY NOT ONE ENTRYPOINT (the option NOT taken, stated because a reviewer will ask). The readers legitimately want different answers and one of them must NOT merge: page_section_satisfiability PREDICTS the loader and must mirror its refusal to merge when no tier serves; ensure_page_section_layout acts only when every source is empty, the same case the loader declines; reconcile_site_plan compares plan version to plan version, where a live row belongs to neither; plan_section_counts is a dedup ALLOWANCE whose victims already exclude locked rows. A single function with four callers wanting four answers grows a parameter boolean.

HONEST LIMITS. It reads SOURCE: it proves the call exists, not that it executes on the path that matters (same stated weakness as component_template_writer_coverage_test.go, whose shape this copies, and comments are stripped for the same reason). It cannot see a reader written in another top-level package that this glob does not cover -- the three roots are named in the test and are the ones that hold every reader today.

plan.summary: RFC_033 option 2, ruled by the owner: a source-scan lockstep test so a NEW reader of site_plan_sections must decide, in writing, whether it honours human locks -- rather than the convention that a header comment and a register entry are today. Mutation-proven on both arms.

edits.rationale: Scans three roots for FROM|JOIN site_plan_sections after stripping line comments; a reader must call the merge or be declared with a reason. Three anti-vacuity controls, because a coverage test that can pass by finding nothing is the exact shape it exists to prevent: (1) it fails if it sees NO readers at all (broken detector); (2) it pins the two known merge-callers BY NAME, so deleting the merge from the loader fails here instead of quietly leaving zero offenders; (3) a sibling test refuses a stale exemption (a declared file that no longer reads the table would otherwise cover a future lock-blind read landing in it).

The exemption map IS the deliverable, so each entry states the mechanism, not a shrug. ensure_page_section_layout: acts only when EVERY source is empty, the same case the loader declines to merge; merging would suppress the scaffold and strand the page. page_section_satisfiability: predicts the loader, so it must mirror the loader's refusal, else it promises a build that no-ops (the false promise bugs_closed/177 was filed for). reconcile_site_plan: plan-version-to-plan-version restamp comparison, and its own header says deliberately not against pages.sections; a live locked row is in neither version and would make every locked page read as re-composed for ever. plan_section_counts: a dedup ALLOWANCE denominator whose victim pool already excludes locked rows via the agent-writable predicate, so merging would raise the allowance without adding a candidate and a real duplicate would survive (pin-predicate-is-not-the-pool-predicate applied to a count). check_sectionless_pages: reads the plan for the SIBLING's layout, not the subject's membership.
edits.sketch: "page_section_satisfiability.go": "predicts the loader, so it must mirror the loader's refusal to merge when no tier serves; counting locked rows would promise a build that no-ops",

grounded_in: Council corr 79f70435 (APPROVED, 2026-08-16 15:31Z), architecture seat verbatim: 'MergeLockedPageSlots + LockedPageSlotsSQL become a cross-package contract ... with no single enforced call path -- a future section-list consumer can still be written lock-blind exactly as the original bug arose. Worth an RFC to decide whether this becomes a single mandatory entrypoint rather than a convention.' Same seat: 'Recommend proceeding but opening the RFC in parallel rather than gating this round.'
OWNER RULING 2026-08-17 on RFC_033: go with the lane's recommendation (option 2, the source-scan lockstep; not option 3, one mandatory entrypoint).

MEASURED 2026-08-17 by running the detector over actions/, actions/*/ and datahelpers/: 6 readers of site_plan_sections -- 2 merge (load_page_sections_from_spec, check_section_source_drift), 4 declared lock-blind. A broader detector including pages.sections readers returns ~18 files.

The test found a reader the author's own census had missed on its FIRST RUN: discovery_checks/check_sectionless_pages.go, matched by JOIN where the hand census had grepped only FROM. Recorded in the lane NOTES as the mechanism justifying itself before it shipped.

MUTATION-PROVEN, both arms, with mutations that COMPILE (a build failure would prove nothing about the test's own logic): renaming load_page_sections_from_spec_action.go fails the by-name pin with its own message; adding a new file carrying a plan-sections query fails the offender arm naming that file. Restored and green after each.

Prior art reused rather than invented: component_template_writer_coverage_test.go (the html_template writer census, bugs_closed/285's sibling case) -- same glob-and-declare shape, same withoutLineComments stripper, same stated source-scan weakness.

bugs_closed/285 is fixed AND live AND proven at the artefact: loancalculator.co.uk/index (corr b45d9965, 08-16) and webdesign.uk/contact (corr 352f5703, 08-17), both natural rebuilds, five owner criteria each plus a served-page check.
plan.risks: (1) SOURCE-SCAN, NOT BEHAVIOUR: it proves a call exists, not that it runs on the path that matters. Stated in the file header rather than left for a reviewer to find. (2) The exemption map is a second hand-written census and will rot if nobody re-reads the reasons; the sibling test only checks that each entry is still a reader, not that its reason is still true. (3) Scope choice: cache readers are deliberately NOT covered, which is only safe while the loader keeps writing the merged list to pages.sections -- if that write is ever removed, this test's scoping argument silently becomes wrong, and nothing here would notice. That dependency is named in the header. (4) The three glob roots are a judgement about where readers live; a reader in a package outside them is invisible, and the test cannot tell that case from 'no such reader exists'.
